chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Fletcher rarely revised arrangements
summary: After writing so much, you can hear the result in your head, so Fletcher seldom revised a finished arrangement.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I see. Did he very often revise arrangements after they had been written or was it pretty
Uh-huh. He had it worked out the way he wanted it.

-- a lot of times after you've written so much, you know, you can envision in your mind how it's going to sound, you know, especially if you have the caliber of musicians with the tone, you know, and execution. You can just see that thing, you know, the way it's going to sound. So you don't have to disturb the arrangement once it's written (unintelligible). That way, you know.
